# Phase 5 tables (generated by `experiments/phase5/5c_tables.py`; do not edit by hand)

All numbers: four-element isotropic array, actual Phase 4 res-30 transfer functions unless stated, inside mask_common (0.231-0.268; domain-limited, post hoc upper edge). Power = |AF|^2/16. Angles in degrees. "Trimmed" always means phase-intercept-trimmed PhC (one constant phase per channel at f0), never ideal TTD.

## Table H. Illustrative normalized-to-physical mapping (carrier = the wave being beamformed; 2-D lossless model, not a manufacturable device)

f_normalized = a/lambda0 = 0.2495 so lambda0 = 4.008 a. One-period delay = channel increment = 3.9323 a/c (Phase 4: one extra period per channel). Pitch from the Phase 5 matching d = c dtau / sin(theta0) = 7.8646 a. Device section length N = 8-11 periods (excluding the 6-period reference spans).

| scaling | free-space lambda0 | lattice constant a | one-period delay | channel increment dtau | array pitch d | N = 8 - 11 section length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. microwave: carrier 30 GHz | 9.993 mm | 2.493 mm | 32.70 ps | 32.70 ps | 19.609 mm | 19.946 mm - 27.426 mm |
| A2. mm-wave: carrier 94 GHz | 3.189 mm | 0.796 mm | 10.44 ps | 10.44 ps | 6.258 mm | 6.366 mm - 8.753 mm |
| B. optical phased array: carrier 1550 nm | 1.550 um | 0.387 um | 5.07 fs | 5.07 fs | 3.041 um | 3.094 um - 4.254 um |

RF-photonic caveat (photonic carrier vs RF beamforming frequency): in a 1550 nm photonic system the lattice constant is 386.7 nm and one period delays the modulation envelope by 5.07 fs. Steering a 30 GHz RF array with half-wave pitch (d = 5 mm, theta0 = 30 deg) needs an incremental delay d sin(theta0)/c = 8.34 ps, i.e. about 1643 periods per element step (635 um), if the same group delay per period held for such long sections (not demonstrated). The Phase 5 one-period matching therefore describes an optical-carrier phased array (the beamformed wave is the PhC carrier), not an RF array fed by this channel family; the RF-photonic use needs much longer or slower delay sections, and the optical-carrier phase intercept is irrelevant there, since the RF phase is set by the envelope delay.
